newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Freeport-McMoran says based on early drilling results, Bre-X Minerals Busang gold field contains "insignificant" amounts of gold.
* John Bennett, founder of New Era Philanthopy, pleaded no contest to charges he defrauded churches, colleges and charities of $135 million.
* Norfolk Southern is set to buy more than half of Conrail's routes, spending $700 million more than expected splitting CSX and Conrail.
* The Nasdaq Composite Index finished up 21.02 points at 1269.08 as technology stocks recovered.
* The dollar, which rose in anticipation of a rate hike, is seen hurting multinational companies' first quarter results.
* After the Fed's short-term rate increase, adjustable-rate mortgages are expected to get more costly.
* Durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February.
* Green Tree Financial Chief Executive Lawrence Coss got a $102 million bonus in 1996.
* The American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) is set to start marketing a variable-annuity product underwritten by Hartford Life next month.
* Group led by SBC Communications intends to pend $1.26 billion for 30 percent stake in Telekom South Africa.
* The U.S. Justice Department said Swiss chemical companies Hoffman-La Roche and Jungbunzlauer agreed to plead guilty in a citric acid price fixing scheme.
* A proposed purchase of Repap was rejected by Avenor stockholders.
* The Motley Fool investment forum on America Online intends to hire its own staff.
* Great Western recieved a higher offer from H.F. Ahmanson but backed its $6.36 billion sale to Washington Mutual.
* Heard on the Street: If all goes according to plan, the nation's biggest provider of variable-annuities is about to get stronger still.

* Credit markets: Bond prices fell in heavy trading, driving the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond briefly over the psychologically important seven percent level, as investors continued to digest Tuesday's interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve -- and also to focus on the potential need for further rate increases.
